Independently differentiated the scalar factors: r'=(2t-3)/(1-t^2)^(3/2); h'=-(1+t^2+2t^3)/(t^2(1-t^2)^(3/2)), equal to the displayed source derivative. Both complete functions strictly decrease, including epsilon=-1 where x>=pi/2 dominates the increasing x factor. G-F=x(1/t-4)/sqrt(1-t^2)>0. At t=1/4 both tend to sqrt(5/3)(x_m-epsilon arcsin(1/4)); at zero F tends to 2x_m and G to infinity. Thus one nonempty interval exists exactly above the strict threshold. Counting integers m>=0 with m<R gives max(0,ceil R), including integer R. This is a universal analytic proof, not finite sampling. Only GC2 components are classified; GC1 still has infinitely many gaps.
